title: Cyber Governance: The Missing Layer in Smart Building Strategy
summary: Strengthen smart building cybersecurity with governance strategies that help real estate leaders manage risk, vendors and connected systems.
body_markdown:
*This article is part three of a three-part series exploring how AI and smart building technologies are reshaping cybersecurity risk, governance, and competitive advantage in real estate.*


- **Article 1:**[Smart Building Cybersecurity: The Risk Behind the Technology](https://www.cbiz.com/insights/article/smart-building-cybersecurity-the-risk-behind-the-technology)
- **Article 2:**[When Smart Buildings Become Cyber Targets](https://www.cbiz.com/insights/article/when-smart-buildings-become-cyber-targets)
- **Article 3:** Cyber Governance: The Missing Layer in Smart Building Strategy


The core challenge facing many real estate organizations isn’t a lack of technology. It’s the absence of a governance framework that links technology, operations, vendors, and risk management. Smart building systems make things more efficient, but without clear accountability, they can also create risks across the portfolio.


## Why Governance Breaks Down


In many organizations, cybersecurity responsibilities are fragmented. Facilities teams manage building systems but may lack cybersecurity experience. IT teams oversee enterprise networks but often lack visibility into operational technology. Vendors and integrators know their platforms, but they may not manage how those platforms integrate with other systems. This separation leaves well-intentioned teams working in silos, with blurred accountability and rising risk.


## Three Pillars of Smart Building Cyber Governance


- **Understand what you have:** Identify what property and tenant data is collected, how it moves, which systems are connected, and where vulnerabilities exist.
- **Evaluate whether it’s enough:** Conduct regular risk assessments, vulnerability testing, and control validation against recognized frameworks.
- **Verify and demonstrate performance:** Use monitoring, logging, third-party checks, incident response plans, and leadership reports to confirm governance is working.


The governance conversation should shift from reactive to strategic. Real estate organizations should integrate cybersecurity into investment decisions, risk management, vendor selection, and performance tracking rather than add it after technology projects are complete.


## The Role of Cybersecurity Advisory Partners


Smart building cybersecurity is complex, spanning IT, operational technology, data privacy, vendor management, compliance, and AI governance. Most real estate organizations can’t build that capability quickly or efficiently on their own. Experienced cybersecurity advisors can help leaders assess risk objectively, accelerate maturity, evaluate third-party exposure, prepare board and investor reporting, and strengthen incident response readiness.


## Five Steps Real Estate Leaders Should Take Now


- **Know what you have.** Build a complete inventory of connected devices, automation systems, IoT sensors, cloud platforms, remote access points, and vendor connections.
- **Assess your risk honestly.** Evaluate IT and OT environments, governance structure, vendor practices, incident response readiness, and alignment with recognized frameworks.
- **Segment your networks.** Separate building automation and IoT systems from tenant networks, enterprise IT, and financial systems.
- **Establish governance and accountability.** Define policies, ownership, reporting, and decision-making processes that span IT, facilities, OT, and vendor management.
- **Build resilience before you need it.** Develop and test incident response plans for smart-building scenarios, including ransomware attacks, access-control failures, and vendor compromises.


## Resilience as a Competitive Advantage


Smart buildings are the norm, not the exception. The question is no longer whether organizations will adopt AI-driven technologies, but whether they will adopt them responsibly and securely. Real estate organizations that define the attack surface early, invest in governance alongside innovation, and work with experienced advisors will be better positioned to protect assets, satisfy investors, retain tenants, and preserve long-term portfolio value.


In a more intelligently built environment, resilience and trust matter as much as efficiency and automation. Organizations that understand this can turn cybersecurity governance into a competitive advantage.


Connect with a member of our team to discuss how your organization can assess smart building cyber risk and strengthen operational resilience.


## Frequently Asked Questions


Smart building technology can improve efficiency, automation, and the tenant experience, but it also expands an organization’s cyber risk profile. A governance framework connects technology decisions to risk management, operations, vendor oversight, and accountability so real estate leaders can adopt connected systems responsibly and securely.


Governance often breaks down when IT, facilities, operational technology teams, vendors, and integrators share responsibility without clear ownership. When each group manages only part of the environment, organizations can lose visibility into connected systems, vendor access, data flows, and portfolio-level vulnerabilities.


Leaders should start with visibility. A complete inventory of connected devices, automation systems, IoT sensors, cloud platforms, remote access points, and vendor connections helps organizations understand their exposure. From there, they can assess risk, segment networks, define accountability, and test incident response plans before a disruption occurs.
